note: Sizes are for eggs in the shell. USDA SR Legacy count portions (large 50 g and so on) are edible weights without the shell.

citation.title: USDA National Nutrient Database for Standard Reference, Release 28, FOOD_DES.txt: NDB 01123 "Egg, whole, raw, fresh", Ref_Desc "Shell", Refuse 12 (percent)

shell.note: One national figure. Shell share varies with hen age, breed and egg size, and is not measured per egg here.

standards.name: United States (USDA consumer grades)
standards.basis: minimum net weight per dozen; per-egg figures are that weight divided by 12

citation.title: United States Standards, Grades, and Weight Classes for Shell Eggs, AMS 56, effective July 20, 2000, section 56.218 (Weight classes), Table I

standards.derivation: minGramsPerEgg = ounces per dozen / 12 x 28.349523125 g; maxGramsPerEggExclusive is the minimum of the next larger class

standards.name: Canada (Canada A)

citation.title: Canadian Grade Compendium, Volume 5 - Eggs, section 5, Table for Size Designations for Canada A Eggs (CFIA)

standards.derivation: Column 2, "Egg weighs not less than". Peewee is read as under 42 g: the page text does not show which column holds its 42 g.

standards.name: European Union (Class A)

citation.title: Commission Regulation (EC) No 589/2008, Article 4: Grading of Class A eggs by weight

standards.derivation: XL 73 g or more; L 63 g or more and under 73 g; M 53 g or more and under 63 g; S under 53 g. The URL is the legislation.gov.uk copy that was read.

notAvailable.reason: No Australian size standard could be found and read. Secondary pages quote ranges, but the Australian Eggs labelling guide itself was not reached, so none are included.
